title: Intelligent eviction-aware admission proxy with weighted queue cascades
creator: Anika Shah
description: Problem: During sudden load shifts dedicated pools can meet throughput commitments for high-priority tenants but cause cascading evictions and long tail latency for best-effort tenants. Current admission components consider only request rate and token cost; they do not account for node-level eviction risk or autoscaler cooldowns. Goal: Build an admission proxy layer that is eviction-aware (uses node eviction risk signal and autoscaler state), implements weighted queue cascades across priority lanes, and enforces per-tenant throughput guarantees while preserving headroom for autoscaler warm-up and low-p99 latency for critical routes. This ticket covers design, prototype, canary rollout, and integration with the dedicated autoscaler and console metrics. The proxy should operate as a thin pre-routing filter (sidecar or edge gateway hook) and expose control knobs for: per-tenant max in-flight, weighted token queue allocations, probabilistic drop thresholds under soft overload, eviction-safe scheduling (prefer delaying to evicting when warmup is in progress), and a backpressure signal to callers for graceful retry or fallback to hosted variants.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Functional: Admission proxy accepts per-tenant policies and enforces weighted queue allocation so that tenants with guaranteed throughput retain their reserved QPS within 95% over a 5-minute window under synthetic overload.

2) Eviction-aware behavior: When node eviction risk metric > 0.6, proxy must reduce new head-of-line assignments to nodes marked at-risk and prioritize queuing to nodes with lower risk. Documented tests validate that this reduces host-level eviction events by at least 30% in chaos scenarios.

3) Autoscaler coordination: When autoscaler signals 'scale up pending', the proxy keeps an autoscaler-headroom budget for new in-flight requests to allow warmup. Metrics must show warmup requests succeed at least 90% without causing host evictions.

4) Latency SLOs: For P0 routes marked 'latency-critical' p99 must remain within existing SLO + 10ms during canary traffic; for non-critical routes p99 increase must be bounded to no more than 2x baseline in overload tests.

5) Observability: Console dashboards must include per-tenant admitted / queued / dropped counts, node-eviction-risk histogram, autoscaler state, and recent decisions with sample request ids. New alerts for 'excessive drops' and 'eviction-likely backlog' must be wired.
6) Safety: Feature toggles must allow per-cluster or per-tenant rollout and a circuit-breaker to revert to current stateless admission. Integration tests and a canary plan documented in the ticket.
7) Documentation: Design doc and operator runbook published in Confluence/Drive with rollback steps and recommended knob settings for common customer profiles.

testing_plan: Unit tests for policy evaluator and queue accounting (target 95% coverage)
E2E tests in staging with synthetic tenants that assert throughput guarantees and queue behavior
Chaos tests: simulated node drains and eviction flaps to verify eviction-aware routing reduces evictions
Canary metrics: admitted_qps, queued_count, dropped_count, node_eviction_events, autoscaler_state_transitions
Load tests: 1x, 3x, and 6x baseline per-pool load to validate degradation profiles
rollout_notes: Start with internal staging traffic, enable for two non-critical external tenants for 72h, monitor metrics and alarms, then graduated rollout. If 'eviction-likely backlog' alert fires or customer-reported errors spike above threshold, flip feature toggle off and notify SRE and PM. Operator runbook links are in the design doc.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: 1) Conservative queuing reduces evictions but increases queue latency for best-effort tenants. 2) Probabilistic drop reduces queue growth with better headroom but can impact tail quality for batched requests. We decided to default to queuing with an aggressive drop threshold only when node eviction risk is high and autoscaler cooldown exceeds configured window. Next step: security review and final PR approvals.
